subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should Slack hosted deployments be steered toward HTTP Request URLs for lower latency through docs/setup guidance, or should OpenClaw change Slack setup/default behavior beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists and the remaining measured gap is mostly outside OpenClaw code, but changing guidance or defaults affects setup expectations, ingress requirements, and existing Socket Mode workflows.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and explicitly recommend HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

options.title: Change setup or defaults
options.body: Sponsor a stronger setup/default change that nudges new hosted Slack installs away from Socket Mode, with upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Record that the existing transport table is sufficient and close only after maintainers decide no latency-specific docs or setup change is planned.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and explicitly recommend HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the measurement and merged partial fix, then explicitly scoped the remaining work to HTTP mode guidance.
